reference: Each of the twenty complete original/native/four-orbit/four-street sheets was individually inspected. Ratings are structural screenings, not aesthetic/runtime acceptance. No original sea wave fringe is masked out or reclassified into the bank model.

river_bank_shore_study_arctic_offset37.defect: The original cool gray-green shore return is softer and narrower; the new angular pale toe forms a continuous heavy strip. Street views expose stair-stepped longitudinal bands rather than the irregular source edge; original blue wave pixels remain independently unresolved.

river_bank_shore_study_arctic_offset39.defect: The opposite Arctic shore has an overly straight tan lower course and uniformly broad shoulder. Native registration retains the source datum but the right endpoint and mottled cold face paint differ; exposed street faces form repetitive terraces.

river_bank_shore_study_arctic_offset48.defect: This diagonal cold owner is continuous and thin, but its white-gray source top is replaced by olive turf and yellow-gray sediment. The toe is too regular and the street return is stair-stepped; wave/foam ownership has not been newly established.

river_bank_shore_study_arctic_offset50.defect: The source has a pale broken return and a separate blue fringe; this model has a uniform dark olive strip with a thick tan lower edge. The far endpoint and street shoulder profile remain angular and the original white/cool paint is not reproduced.

river_bank_shore_study_temperate_offset1.defect: The near temperate sloping bank is now a connected irregular-width soil/turf shell, but its toe is too pale and its green crest too straight. Native left-end shape and rust-colored waterline paint differ; orbit/street views expose repeated horizontal erosion courses.

The opposing temperate slope retains a thin continuous volume, yet the source shoulder is softer and less uniform. The bank-only native underfills the central rough lobe and omits source red-brown edge tones; the long street face is overly terraced.

river_bank_shore_study_temperate_offset2.defect: The rising diagonal has a manually broken toe and turf cap but the source's fragmented far tip and warm shoreline accents are not reproduced. Native top width is too uniform, and the broad exposed pale sediment strips remain unlike the original soil.

This opposing diagonal keeps the original slope and bank thickness, but the lower course is too regular and continuous. The green upper return and native endpoint placement do not match the finer original source edge; street bands are conspicuous.

river_bank_shore_study_temperate_offset3.defect: The descending temperate return has genuine connected soil/turf relief, but its outer pale ledge is too wide and its crest too straight. The source has broken brown/green shoulder paint and a distinct water fringe; street terraces and native tip mismatch remain.

The opposite descending owner is structurally complete but the source's rounded end lobe becomes an angular narrow point. Soil/turf contrast and warm near-water face accents remain inaccurate, and orbit/street views expose repeated longitudinal courses.

river_bank_shore_study_tropic_offset12.defect: The tropical near shore forms a connected thin bank but its beige toe contrasts too sharply with the dark green turf. The source edge has warm rust patches and a softer irregular shoulder; repeated terrace bands and wrong endpoint silhouette remain.

river_bank_shore_study_tropic_offset14.defect: The opposing tropical bank retains the original slope but the source's low lobes and reddish waterline are simplified into regular pale shelves. Native green registration and tip width differ, and street cuts expose a uniform layered ramp rather than eroded ground.

river_bank_shore_study_tropic_offset37.defect: The descending tropical shoulder is occupied throughout, but its straight green cap and continuous cream outer ledge do not match the dark mottled, warm-edged original. The native centre and far tip underfill the source bank shape; street terraces remain too regular.

river_bank_shore_study_tropic_offset39.defect: This tropical return preserves thin relief, but its pointed high endpoint and low toe course disagree with the rounded source shoulder. The original dark green/rust edge paint is replaced by an overly pale sediment band; long street faces remain regularly stepped.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset12.defect: The original ochre near shore is broken by beige, green and rust islands; the new volume has a nearly uninterrupted bright golden crest. Native endpoint and pale toe width differ, and street terraces are much more uniform than the source's toy-ground paint.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset14.defect: The opposite Toyland bank is continuous but too uniformly yellow and cream. It loses the source's green shoulder interruption and warm reddish return near the water; native upper profile and street bands remain strongly angular.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset25.defect: The source diagonal has alternating beige/olive and ochre patches and a small warm wave-end return; this model replaces them with a continuous yellow stripe. The native high tip is too solid and street-facing lower courses too regular.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset27.defect: This opposing Toyland slope has a solid thin shell, but its golden crest and olive toe are overly continuous. Source shoulder islands and rust endpoint paint are missing; the native low tip and repeated street erosion courses do not reproduce the original.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset37.defect: The descending ochre shore volume is wider and more regular than the mottled source. Native far-tip shape and pale/green return placement disagree, while four orbit and street views show conspicuous straight golden and cream terrace strips.

river_bank_shore_study_toyland_offset39.defect: The original opposite shore is broken into ochre, green and warm beige patches; this candidate retains an almost uninterrupted golden crest. The angular upper tip, pale continuous toe and regularly stepped street faces remain unlike the source.
